properties.name: An exposed reflow2 verifies OAuth bearer tokens itself, and the caller is the Contributor the operator's mapping derives from the verified token
properties.rationale:
CAUSE (fact:root-cause-an-exposed-server-accepts-any-callers-signature-because-the-boundary-where-write-rules-attach-was-named-and-no-rule-was-chosen-2026-09-28): an exposed server took any caller's signature because the boundary where write rules attach was named and no rule chosen. The ruling dec:idea-authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer-and-the-line-is-the-contributor-id (option (e), Anthony 2026-09-28: "Go with the solution that is most right. I don't like quick or patch efforts that don't fix at root") gives every exposure a rule. #636 built the enforcement half (the Signer, the trusted gateway, the undeclared fallback) and said the bearer half was owed, "CallerRule takes it as one more variant"; until now an exposed --http engine with no gateway could only read and propose, so a team behind its own identity provider could not approve from its server. This builds that variant, to the floor of req:every-oauth-role-reflow2-plays-meets-oauth-2-1-at-a-minimum, so the person is established by a token reflow2 checks itself — no trusted header in the path. Anthony 2026-10-01 made finishing the OAuth 2.1 work the priority.

CHOICES TAKEN at build time (the capability's OPEN SUB-CHOICES): flags --http-oidc-issuer, --http-public-url, --http-oidc-audience, --http-oidc-jwks-uri, --http-oidc-jwks-file, --http-oidc-required-scope, --http-oidc-required-claim, --http-contributor-id, --http-contributor-map; a vetted JWT crate (jsonwebtoken, default features off) over hand-rolled JOSE, with ring as its provider so the binary keeps one crypto stack and takes neither aws-lc-rs nor the rsa crate (RUSTSEC-2023-0071); a JWKS GET sibling in mcp_http.rs. The image's "NO AUTHENTICATION" label is still left for #617.

NETWORK I/O: fetching a key set is network I/O. No accepted rule forbids it (fact:the-sentence-reflow2-does-no-network-io-by-principle-is-not-an-accepted-rule-and-has-been-untrue-since-the-remote-client-2026-10-01); the fetch target is only ever the operator's configuration, and --http-oidc-jwks-file serves a deployment that must not reach out.

OBSERVED FAILING FIRST on origin/main dd9626d (2026-10-01, own target dir, shared build lock; the test file and fixture untracked in a detached worktree, with ring and base64 added as dev-dependencies only so it could compile): 15 of the 16 tests then in the file failed (log: bearer-failfirst.log in the session scratchpad). 13 failed because the server would not start: "error: unexpected argument --http-public-url found" — main had no resource-server mode. The startup-refusal test failed because --http-oidc-issuer was an unknown flag rather than refused with a reason; the TLS test failed because --help said nothing about TLS. The 16th, loopback_http_without_an_issuer_takes_no_token, passed on main as it must: it pins behaviour that does not change. The 17th, a_recovered_resource_server_still_verifies_every_token, was written after #620 merged; it was shown red by a mutation run (the recovered door built without the verifier) and green on the true source.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: New crates/reflow2-mcp/src/bearer.rs: an OAuth 2.0 resource server. BearerGate (a tower service inside the Host gate, in front of the single design, the registry router and the degraded surface) serves /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (RFC 9728), refuses a token in the URI query string (400) and a malformed Authorization header (400), verifies the Bearer JWT (jsonwebtoken with ring as its verify-only crypto provider; RS/PS/ES256/ES384/EdDSA only; none, HS* and an alg that does not fit its key refused; iss exact, aud = this resource by default, exp required, nbf), enforces --http-oidc-required-scope / --http-oidc-required-claim (403 insufficient_scope), answers every refusal with a Bearer challenge carrying resource_metadata, derives the contributor through the operator's --http-contributor-id template and optional --http-contributor-map, removes the Authorization header, binds each MCP session to the sign-in that opened it, and hands a VerifiedCaller to the MCP service in the request's extensions. Keys: OpenID discovery (then RFC 8414) at the operator's issuer, --http-oidc-jwks-uri, or a pinned --http-oidc-jwks-file; cached by kid, refreshed after 10 minutes or at once for an unknown kid (at most once per 30 s); a token's jku/x5u/jwk are never followed. caller.rs: CallerRule::BearerToken — the verified token's contributor is the caller, a _meta["reflow2/writes_for"] or writes_for naming anyone else is refused, and #636's Signer holds every AUTHORED_BY to them. main.rs: the flags, startup refusals (stdio, --shared, beside --http-trusted-gateway, no mapping, no public URL, a non-loopback http:// public URL), and a banner stating that reflow2 does not terminate TLS. mcp_http.rs: get_json, a bounded GET that follows no redirect. Docs: CHANGELOG, collaborating.md.
